entities.summary: Humbeline of Jully was a Benedictine nun in 11th-12th century France, known for her remarkable life and legacy. Born into a noble family, Humbeline was ordained as a nun at a young age and dedicated her life to prayer and service. She was a member of the Cluny Order, a prominent Benedictine abbey in the region, and was recognized for her piety and devotion. In 1141, Humbeline died at the age of approximately 50, leaving behind a lasting impact on the lives of those who knew her. Her beatification by Pope Clement XI in 1703 marked the beginning of her canonization, solidifying her place in the annals of Catholic history. Humbeline's story serves as a testament to the enduring power of faith and the importance of women's roles in shaping the course of history. As a symbol of devotion and service, Humbeline of Jully continues to inspire generations of Catholics and history enthusiasts alike.
